title: Node.js 18 support removed in Next.js 16
statement: Next.js 16 raises the minimum Node.js version to 20.9.0 and no longer supports Node.js 18.
sourceEvidence: Runtime support table: “Node.js 20.9+” and “Node.js 18 no longer supported.”

title: Middleware convention renamed to Proxy in Next.js 16
statement: The middleware filename and named export are deprecated and renamed to proxy; the upgrade guide supplies the rename and notes the Edge runtime caveat.
sourceEvidence: Section “middleware to proxy”: filename and export rename instructions; “The edge runtime is NOT supported in proxy.”

title: Experimental PPR configuration changed in Next.js 16
statement: Next.js 16 removes the experimental Partial Prerendering flag/configuration options, including experimental_ppr; PPR behavior and migration guidance differ from Next.js 15 canaries.
sourceEvidence: The guide says Next.js 16 removes “the experimental Partial Prerendering (PPR) flag and configuration options, including the route level experimental_ppr.” It says PPR in Next.js 15 canaries works differently and advises staying on the current canary.

title: Dynamic request APIs became asynchronous in Next.js 15
statement: Next.js 15 changes cookies, headers, draftMode, params, and searchParams APIs from synchronous access to asynchronous APIs, with a codemod and temporary synchronous access path documented.
sourceEvidence: Section “Async Request APIs”: lists cookies, headers, draftMode, params, and searchParams; says a codemod and temporary synchronous access are available.
